speaker: john_shakespeare
text: I don't go because Master Bailiff's man stands at the porch with paper, and I've no wish to read it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The paper's lighter than it was, Father.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Is it so? Then some fairy's been at my reckoning. I'll not thank a fairy. It spoils them.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Your father has told the better half of that story.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The church will not wait on a fairy. Thy cloak, Will.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: My knees ache less in mine own parlour. Two Sundays is a modest habit for a man who has been bailiff.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have a shop to mind, sir. I asked you straight. I will not ask you twice.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Put the dry gloves above the wet, master. The boys have been at the tub.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: I taught thee to cut a glove, Will. The rest thou hast added at great expense. Go and be patient in a pew.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The shop door shuts. The rest of the house goes down the lane. That is the whole of it.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: I'll take Judith's hand. She will mimic the man if no one has her by the wrist.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Let her hear it. A sermon on patience can bear one true copy.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: By my troth, if the man at the porch has a new sheet, tell him the old one has grown shy.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll tell him nothing, sir. You asked me not to thank the fairy.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: You're thin, son. Eat before the psalms, or patience will be all the dinner you get till noon.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: There is bread on the board. Sit, the three of you, and then we go.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Was it paid, or did a gentleman say it would be?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is lighter, Susanna. That is the whole answer I have.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: A counting child, like thy brother Gilbert. God's my comfort, the house is full of auditors.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: If the fairy paid it, the fairy should come to church and be thanked. You said thanking spoils them. I am applying the rule.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Can he take the sword as far as the lane and not into the porch?

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: No blade in the church lane. Leave it on the nail.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Thou hast ink on thy cuff again, brother. Let me brush it ere Mother sees.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Brush it. I would go in as a son and not as a desk.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Go on, then. Shut my door as you pass. I am not at home to paper.
